reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the order and refund data myself, since the handoff only reports W2's summary and payouts can't be recalled.
The orders list has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). Before computing payouts, I need to verify W2's refund claims against the actual refund records, since payouts can't be undone.
The refund records match W2's claim: order 113 ($7379) and order 115 ($6651). Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 22142 matches my own check: orders 10805 + 18716 = 29521, minus refund 7379. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 49030 matches my check: orders 39303 + 9727, with no refunds. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.
Cobalt's net balance of 33952 matches my check: orders 6135 + 34468 = 40603, minus refund 6651. All three balances agree with my arithmetic, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 22142.
Acme's payout is recorded and its figure matched my own check. Birch's net balance of 49030 also matched my arithmetic, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout is recorded. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance of 33952 matched my own check, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own arithmetic, so the batch is complete.
